merger_description:
Oaktree Capital Holdings, LLC (together with its subsidiaries, **Oaktree**), acting through Vector JV Bidco, a special purpose vehicle it controls, proposes to:

* acquire 100% of the shares issued in each of VXMT Corporation, Vivax (Asia) Ltd, Metrotech Vertriebs GmbH, Vivax Metrotech Sdn. Bhd., Vivax-Metrotech Ltd. and Vivax-Metrotech SAS (together, **Vivax**);
* grant AMI Holding GmbH, the vendor, a 40% indirect equity participation in Vector JV Bidco through the vendor’s investment in Vector JV Topco, Inc. (the **Acquisition**);

As a result of the Acquisition, Oaktree will own a 60% stake in Vivax.

Oaktree is indirectly jointly controlled by Oaktree Capital Group Holdings GP, LLC and Brookfield Corporation (together with its subsidiaries - other than the Oaktree group – **Brookfield Group**).

Oaktree is a global investment manager specialising in alternative investments. Oaktree pursues an opportunistic, value-oriented and risk-controlled approach to investments in distressed debt, high yield bonds, convertible securities, senior loans, corporate control, real estate, emerging market equities and mezzanine finance. Headquartered in Los Angeles, Oaktree has over 1,200 employees and offices in over 22 cities worldwide. Oaktree has investments in a range of companies in Australia including IT businesses and health and wellness food manufacturing, among others.

Brookfield Group is a global investment firm that deploys pools of discretionary capital for investors across its core businesses, including its asset management business and its operating businesses focused on renewable power and transition, infrastructure, private equity, and real estate. Brookfield Group is a public company and its Class A Limited Voting Shares are co-listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol “BN”. Brookfield Group has investments in Australia across a range of sectors, including infrastructure and energy. Brookfield Group is in the process of acquiring the remaining interest in Oaktree.

Vivax is a global surveying instrument manufacturer. Its products are used for locating and mapping buried utilities and inspecting the interior of pipes and ducts. In Australia, Vivax predominantly supplies precision pipes and cable locating equipment and related accessories through an independent third-party distributor. Vivax also provide full calibration of their pipe and cable locaters in Australia.

AMI Holding GmbH is the current Germany-based holding company for Vivax.

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there are no material competitive overlaps between Oaktree,
Brookfield Group and Vivax in the supply of utility services,
and surveying instruments, particularly underground utility
detection equipment in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of surveying instruments,
including underground utility detection equipment in
Australia.
The ACCC has also had regard to the likelihood that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds
determined under section 51ABP(1) of the Act would apply.
While the ACCC considers that the notification thresholds are likely
to be met, given that material competition concerns are unlikely to
arise, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required
to be notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
